risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management explicitly flags that the risk of business slowdown, inadequate growth and negative returns has increased, calling hospitality 'the most affected' industry; its readiness plan (next-generation talent models, data-driven decision making, customer loyalty, operational flexibility) is still, in its own words, awaiting 'the path from theory to action'.
- A security breach would require notifying past and present guests, is costly, damages the brand, and can expose the Company to liability claims for failure to protect data — a risk rising as more hospitality systems are digitised.
- Guests are described as potentially the biggest direct and indirect threat to profitability; lawsuits from injured persons and damage to guestrooms are a stated risk to the bottom line, mitigated only through internal controls and closer management of property.
- Maintaining high and consistent standards is described as challenging due to the geographical distance separating each establishment; any infringement by an inferior brand may affect customers' perception, requiring registered IP rights and regular IP audits.
- Cost pressures related to manpower, energy and food inflation remained key considerations for operators during the year, and rising operational costs are named a continuing challenge — direct margin exposure for a single-segment hotel and F&B business.
- Inflationary pressures across major economies, geopolitical uncertainties and currency volatility — particularly a relatively strong US dollar — continued to impact international travel demand and inbound tourism flows in select markets.
- Regional airline capacity remained approximately 8%-12% below pre-pandemic (2019) levels during FY 2025-26, capping international travel volumes until fleet expansion and route additions narrow the gap.
- Rapidly changing customer demands and a boom in guest-facing connected technologies are named as factors changing the sector's risk landscape; without digital and online-marketing capability management says it is increasingly difficult to build a profitable hotel business model.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:

- Customer experience enhancement and strategic expansion aligned with India's long-term tourism-led growth trajectory
- Selective adoption of digital tools — evaluating together with employees which digital helpers offer real added value for guests and genuinely benefit the operation of the hotel units, alongside renewing IT structures and expanding digital communication channels
- Embedding a culture of proactive risk management by supporting acceptable and monitored risk-taking, …
